_comment: Popular packages that pkgxray BLOCKS on a heuristic (non-CVE) finding, where the block is CORRECT/defensible because the package genuinely performs the flagged high-risk operation. These are excluded from the 'heuristic false blocks must be 0' gate the same way known-CVE blocks are — they are true positives a security team SHOULD review, not calibration errors. Each entry must name the exact reason; keep this list minimal and audited. Do NOT add a package here to hide a genuine false positive — fix the detector instead.

packages.pm2: Genuinely installs boot persistence: `lib/API/Startup.js` writes /etc/systemd/system (and upstart/launchd/systemv/openrc) units as its documented `pm2 startup` feature. A process manager that installs system-level boot persistence is exactly what a supply-chain audit should surface for human review; the systemd/init-write BLOCK is the top real-world malware-persistence signal and is deliberately not weakened.
packages.bun: Genuinely downloads and executes a standalone runtime at install time: `install.js` runs `curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash` (and the PowerShell `irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex` on Windows) to fetch the Bun binary from its first-party domain. Install-time download-then-execute of a native binary is exactly the capability a supply-chain audit exists to surface — statically indistinguishable from the TeamPCP bootstrap shape — so it is a true positive a human should confirm, not a false block. The alternate-runtime-exec BLOCK is deliberately not weakened.
packages.firebase-tools: Genuinely reads the project `.env` and feeds its contents to build/deploy processes with network egress: `lib/frameworks/index.js` / `lib/firebase_studio/migrate.js` read `.env`/.env files near framework-build (`child_process`) and upload paths. A deploy CLI that reads your secrets file and can send it to a platform is a real, powerful capability a security reviewer should see; it is statically indistinguishable from a read-then-exfil, so it is a true positive to review, not a calibration error.
